subject.title: [Feature Request] Telegram inline buttons for pairing approve/deny

question: Should Telegram chat callbacks be allowed to approve or deny pairing/device requests, and which operator scopes must a button press prove for DM pairing versus operator.admin browser/device approval?
rationale: The requested UX moves access-changing approval from CLI or scoped gateway approval into Telegram callback handling, and current source preserves a narrower operator.pairing scope for non-gateway Telegram command owners.

options.title: Design typed approval actions
options.body: Define reusable approval actions with request id, action, expiry, single-use semantics, caller identity, and existing scope enforcement before Telegram renders Approve/Deny buttons.

options.title: Limit to DM sender pairing
options.body: Add buttons only for low-scope channel DM pairing and leave operator.admin device/browser approvals on CLI or Control UI until a separate step-up model lands.

options.title: Defer chat-originated approval
options.body: Keep the command-copy workflow until broader channel-aware device approval and step-up authorization direction is settled.

recommendation.title: Design typed approval actions
recommendation.body: Define reusable approval actions with request id, action, expiry, single-use semantics, caller identity, and existing scope enforcement before Telegram renders Approve/Deny buttons.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the clearest routing candidate from the visible current-main history for the shared pairing/device-pair approval surfaces being changed.
